summary.text: 书 is the standardized simplified form of 書. The traditional graph is analyzed as a writing-related compound; regularizing its cursive form changed the visible shape, so it no longer clearly shows that analysis.

formation.text: 書 is traditionally analyzed as phonosemantic: 聿 contributes a writing-related meaning, and 者 is assigned a phonetic role. 书 is the standardized simplified counterpart, formed by regularizing a cursive shape of 書.

components.text: Within 書, 聿 is the semantic element associated with writing. The supplied historical comparison glosses it as a writing stylus or brush, but does not establish its original pictorial form.

Within 書, 者 is assigned the phonetic role in the traditional analysis. Baxter–Sagart gives readings for both graphs in the same system, but they do not by themselves explain the historical sound relation.

sound_limitation.text: Baxter–Sagart gives 書 as MC syo / OC *s-ta and 者 as MC tsyaeX / OC *tAʔ. Their Old Chinese initials differ, and these values alone do not explain or establish the historical phonetic relation assigned in the traditional analysis.

sound.text: In Modern Mandarin, 者 is zhě and 書 is shū. This present-day pair does not establish their historical phonetic relationship.

history.text: 書 is traditionally analyzed as composed of 聿 and 者, with the latter assigned the sound role. The simplified 书 regularizes a cursive form of 書; this graphic account does not establish that 书 depicts a hand holding a brush.
The supplied seal-style and bronze-style images are modern redraws. Their labels do not independently date the forms or establish a sequence of graphic development.

uncertainties.text: The earliest securely dated attestation of 書 and a dated sequence of its historical forms remain unresolved in the cited evidence.
The traditional analysis assigns 者 a phonetic role, but the supplied Baxter–Sagart readings do not explain the historical correspondence: their Old Chinese initials differ.

senses.text: The traditional gloss associates 書 with writing or setting something down; the evidence does not identify this as the earliest attested use.
書 is also used to mean “record.” The cited example does not establish when this use arose relative to the other senses.
The character is used for writing or text; cited examples do not date this sense in relation to the others.
“Book” is a current meaning of the character and also occurs in cited classical examples. The evidence does not date its development from “write” or “text.”
書 also means “letter” or “document.” The cited examples do not establish when these uses arose or how they relate chronologically to the other senses.

limitations.text: The cited examples attest several uses, but do not establish a chronological path among writing, recording, text, book, letter and document.

overview.text: 书 is the simplified form of 書, traditionally analyzed as a writing-related compound: 聿 contributes the writing meaning, while 者 is assigned a sound role. The simplified graph comes from regularizing a cursive form.

components.text: In 書, 聿 is the writing-related element.
In 書, 者 is assigned the sound role; its modern reading does not explain the historical relationship.

relationships.text: 书 is the standardized simplified form of 書, described as regularizing a cursive form into standard script.
In the traditional analysis of 書, 聿 contributes the writing-related meaning.

The traditional analysis assigns 者 the phonetic role in 書. Modern Mandarin gives 者 zhě and 書 shū; the Baxter–Sagart comparison gives MC tsyaeX / syo and OC *tAʔ / *s-ta. The Old Chinese initials differ, and these readings alone do not explain the historical assignment.
